title: Space Commerce Advisory Committee Act

claims.claim: Creates a federal advisory committee
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary shall establish a Commercial Space Activity Advisory Committee

claims.claim: The committee is characterized as a 'standing' committee
claims.note: Source establishes a committee with a 10-year sunset (SEC 3(d)); 'standing' loosely implies permanence. Non-material — the same summary states the sunset.

claims.claim: inside the Commerce Department's Office of Space Commerce
claims.sourceSpan: means the Secretary of Commerce, acting through the Office of Space Commerce
claims.note: Secretary defined as Secretary of Commerce acting through the Office of Space Commerce; committee established by the Secretary.

claims.claim: to advise on nongovernmental space activities
claims.sourceSpan: to advise on the status and recent developments of nongovernmental space activities

claims.claim: required to be stood up within 180 days of enactment
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish a Commercial Space Activity Advisory Committee

claims.claim: will have 15 members drawn from the commercial space industry
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall be composed of 15 members appointed by the Secretary
claims.note: 15 members; commercial-space experience per 3(b)(2)(A).

claims.claim: with a general bar on federal employees
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary may not appoint as a member of the Committee any employee or official of the Federal Government
claims.note: Polarity check: prohibition/bar direction correct.

claims.claim: advise the Secretary and Congress on competitiveness, export controls, radio-frequency spectrum, planetary protection best practices, and international obligations
claims.sourceSpan: to provide to the Secretary and Congress recommendations
claims.note: All five subjects sourced across duties (2),(3)(A-D),(4).

claims.claim: set to terminate ten years after it is established
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall terminate on the date that is 10 years after the date on which the Committee is established

claims.claim: 15-member Commerce Department advisory committee on commercial space activities
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall be composed of 15 members appointed by the Secretary

claims.claim: 180-day standup deadline
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: 10-year sunset
claims.sourceSpan: 10 years after the date on which the Committee is established

claims.claim: New Advisory Committee at Commerce
claims.sourceSpan: establish a Commercial Space Activity Advisory Committee

claims.claim: Established by the Secretary of Commerce acting through the Office of Space Commerce
claims.sourceSpan: means the Secretary of Commerce, acting through the Office of Space Commerce

claims.claim: Must be stood up within 180 days after enactment
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Sunsets 10 years after establishment
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall terminate on the date that is 10 years after the date on which the Committee is established
claims.note: Polarity check: runs from establishment (not enactment) — correct.

claims.claim: 15 members appointed by the Secretary
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall be composed of 15 members appointed by the Secretary

claims.claim: Drawn from space policy, engineering, technical, science, legal, academic, and finance fields
claims.sourceSpan: space policy, engineering, technical, science, legal, academic, and finance fields who have significant experience in the commercial space industry

claims.claim: Generally no federal employees; sole exception is special government employees already serving on other federal advisory committees
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary may appoint as a member of the Committee a special government employee (as defined in section 202(a) of title 18, United States Code) who serves on 1 or more other Federal advisory committees
claims.note: 'sole exception' accurate — it is the only carve-out to the federal-employee bar.

claims.claim: Term limit: up to 4 years, with a 2-year cooling-off period afterward
claims.sourceSpan: shall be appointed for a term of not more than 4 years
claims.note: 2-year cooling-off per 3(b)(3)(B).

claims.claim: Recommendations on facilitating a competitive, safe, sustainable, innovative U.S. commercial space sector
claims.sourceSpan: safe, sustainable, robust, competitive, and innovative commercial sector
claims.note: Each listed adjective is sourced; analysis drops the modifier 'robust' — non-material.

claims.claim: Advise on export controls affecting commercial space, harmful interference in outer space, and access to radio-frequency spectrum
claims.sourceSpan: export controls that affect the commercial space sector
claims.note: Harmful interference 3(c)(3)(C); spectrum 3(c)(3)(D).

claims.claim: Review best practices to avoid harmful contamination of the Moon and other celestial bodies
claims.sourceSpan: the harmful contamination of the Moon and other celestial bodies

claims.claim: Review best practices to avoid adverse changes in Earth's environment from extraterrestrial matter
claims.sourceSpan: adverse changes in the environment of the Earth resulting from the introduction of extraterrestrial matter

claims.claim: Defines 'Secretary' as the Secretary of Commerce acting through the Office of Space Commerce
claims.sourceSpan: means the Secretary of Commerce, acting through the Office of Space Commerce

claims.claim: defines 'State' broadly to include the District of Columbia and all U.S. territories
claims.sourceSpan: the District of Columbia
claims.note: 'all U.S. territories' fairly glosses PR, USVI, Guam, American Samoa, CNMI, and any other commonwealth/territory/possession.

claims.claim: 'United States entity' as a U.S. national (as defined in section 101(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act)
claims.sourceSpan: an individual who is a national of the United States (as defined in section 101(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act

claims.claim: or a nongovernmental entity organized under U.S. or state law
claims.sourceSpan: a nongovernmental entity organized or existing under, and subject to, the laws of the United States or a State
claims.note: Source joins (A)/(B) with 'and'; categories are mutually exclusive (individual vs. entity), so the analysis's 'either/or' reading is correct.

claims.claim: Directs the Secretary to establish a Commercial Space Activity Advisory Committee within 180 days after enactment
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish a Commercial Space Activity Advisory Committee

claims.claim: The committee will have 15 members appointed by the Secretary
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall be composed of 15 members appointed by the Secretary

claims.claim: Members must come from space policy, engineering, technical, science, legal, academic, or finance fields with significant experience in the commercial space industry (which may include prior government experience)
claims.sourceSpan: space policy, engineering, technical, science, legal, academic, and finance fields who have significant experience in the commercial space industry, which may include previous Government experience

claims.claim: Except for special government employees already serving on other federal advisory committees, the Secretary may not appoint any federal employee or official as a member
claims.sourceSpan: Except as provided in clause (ii), the Secretary may not appoint as a member of the Committee any employee or official of the Federal Government
claims.note: Polarity + exception scope both correct.

claims.claim: Sets a 4-year term limit with a 2-year cooling-off period
claims.sourceSpan: shall be appointed for a term of not more than 4 years

claims.claim: Each member serves for up to 4 years, and during the 2-year period after that term ends may not serve again on the committee
claims.sourceSpan: during the 2-year period beginning on the date on which such term ends, may not serve as a member of the Committee

claims.claim: Lists five duty areas: status of the sector, competitiveness recommendations, sector challenges, planetary-protection best practices, and other advice
claims.sourceSpan: The duties of the Committee shall be
claims.note: Duties enumerated (1)-(5) = five; mapping to the five listed areas is faithful.

claims.claim: The sector-challenges brief specifically names four topics: international obligations, export controls, harmful interference in outer space, and access to adequate, predictable, and reliable radio-frequency spectrum
claims.sourceSpan: access to adequate, predictable, and reliable radio frequency spectrum
claims.note: Four topics = subparts (A)-(D); all four sourced.

claims.claim: The planetary-protection duty asks the committee to review best practices for U.S. entities to avoid harmful contamination of the Moon and other celestial bodies, and adverse changes in Earth's environment from the introduction of extraterrestrial matter
claims.sourceSpan: to review existing best practices for United States entities to avoid
claims.note: Both prongs (4)(A) and (4)(B) sourced.

claims.claim: Terminates the committee 10 years after it is established
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall terminate on the date that is 10 years after the date on which the Committee is established

claims.claim: The 10-year sunset runs from establishment rather than enactment
claims.sourceSpan: 10 years after the date on which the Committee is established
claims.note: Correctly distinguishes establishment vs. enactment; downstream inference about end-date timing is a valid deduction.

claims.claim: The committee is charged with reviewing planetary-protection best practices — preventing harmful contamination of the Moon and other celestial bodies, and preventing adverse changes in Earth's environment from extraterrestrial matter
claims.sourceSpan: the harmful contamination of the Moon and other celestial bodies

claims.claim: planetary protection is one of only five explicitly enumerated duty areas
claims.sourceSpan: The duties of the Committee shall be
claims.note: Five enumerated duties (1)-(5).

claims.claim: establishes a 15-member advisory committee but does not authorize appropriations or specify a funding source for its operations
claims.note: Verified by absence: no appropriations or funding-source language anywhere in source.

claims.claim: lists five duty areas but does not require the committee to publish periodic reports or make its recommendations public
claims.note: Verified by absence: duties contain no reporting/publication requirement.

claims.claim: lets the Secretary appoint members without requiring geographic diversity, small-business representation, or academic-versus-industry balance
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall be composed of 15 members appointed by the Secretary
claims.note: Verified by absence: qualifications impose no geographic/small-business/balance requirement.

claims.claim: terminates the committee 10 years after establishment but does not require a review or reauthorization process before that sunset takes effect
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall terminate on the date that is 10 years after the date on which the Committee is established
claims.note: Verified by absence: no review/reauthorization provision.

claims.claim: New Commercial Space Activity Advisory Committee at the Commerce Department's Office of Space Commerce (15 members, 4-year terms, 10-year sunset)
claims.sourceSpan: establish a Commercial Space Activity Advisory Committee
claims.note: 15 members 3(b)(1); 4-year terms 3(b)(3)(A); 10-year sunset 3(d) — all sourced.

claims.claim: Introduced by Sen. Gary Peters (D-MI)
claims.note: Sponsor is structural cache metadata (Congress.gov), permitted by rubric framing rule; not present in bill text.

claims.claim: with 2 cosponsors
claims.note: Cosponsor count is structural cache metadata; not in bill text.

claims.claim: directs the Commerce Department's Office of Space Commerce to stand up a 15-member private-sector advisory committee within 180 days of enactment
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish a Commercial Space Activity Advisory Committee
claims.note: 'private-sector' glossed from the federal-employee bar (3(b)(2)(B)) plus commercial-industry membership (3(b)(2)(A)).

claims.claim: The bill passed the Senate on August 6, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: Passed the Senate August 6, 2026
claims.note: Matches votes[] (Passed by Unanimous Consent 2026-08-06).

claims.claim: and awaits House consideration
claims.note: Structural stage inference from Senate passage; consistent with stage field 'Passed Senate'.

claims.claim: Advisory-committee authorizations of this narrow, non-fiscal form move often but not always
claims.note: 'non-fiscal' supported by absence of appropriations; 'move often but not always' is an uncited likelihood generalization. Non-material.

claims.claim: the ten-year sunset and the ban on federal-employee members are the substantive levers the House may want to revisit
claims.sourceSpan: The Committee shall terminate on the date that is 10 years after the date on which the Committee is established
claims.note: Factual anchors (10-year sunset 3(d); federal-employee ban 3(b)(2)(B)) are sourced; 'levers the House may want to revisit' is non-material speculation.

claims.claim: SGE exception cited as defined in section 202(a) of title 18, U.S. Code — statutory definitional cite dropped by the analysis
claims.sourceSpan: a special government employee (as defined in section 202(a) of title 18, United States Code)
claims.note: Analysis conveys the special-government-employee exception but omits the 18 U.S.C. 202(a) definitional cite. Non-material; substance preserved.

notes: Single-source audit — bill has no registered referencedSources; sole source is data/bill-text/119-S-434.txt (S.434 Engrossed in Senate, 4,674 chars, fully read). All figures (15 members, 180 days, 4-year term, 2-year cooling-off, 10-year sunset, five duties, four challenge topics), entities (Secretary of Commerce/Office of Space Commerce), directions (federal-employee bar, sunset-from-establishment) verified against source. No material errors. Minor items: loose 'standing' descriptor (summary states the sunset anyway), and two non-material likelihood-framing clauses. One non-material omission (18 U.S.C. 202(a) SGE cite).
